complaintTypes.primaryPurpose: Useful primarily as intelligence, surveillance initiation, or background checks.
complaintTypes.keyCaveats: Agencies such as A&N explicitly take NO ACTION on unverified address/anonymous complaints. Others like Haryana use it to start intelligence gathering.

complaintTypes.primaryPurpose: Detailed investigation into ongoing systemic fraud, disproportionate assets, or kickback schemes.
complaintTypes.keyCaveats: Identity is recorded by the agency but withheld from the accused under official secrecy rules.

complaintTypes.primaryPurpose: Catching a public servant red-handed while demanding or accepting an illegal gratification (bribe).
complaintTypes.keyCaveats: Requires an identifiable complainant (or witness representative) to participate in laying chemical/pre-trap evidence, witness verification, and formal testimony.

bribeDemand.title: Immediate Bribe Demand (Current / Active)
steps: DO NOT pay the bribe immediately if you plan to report it.
Contact the State ACB / Vigilance Bureau helpline immediately (e.g. 1064, 14400, or direct headquarters number).
Submit a written complaint detailing who demanded the bribe, for what service, and the location/time.
The ACB/Vigilance team will arrange independent official witnesses and treat currency notes with phenolphthalein powder for a sting/trap operation.

systemicCorruption.title: Systemic Corruption / Large Fraud
systemicCorruption.pathway: State ACB / Vigilance → State Lokayukta → CPGRAMS (Central Portal) → CVC / CBI (if Central Govt involved)
steps: Gather documentary evidence (RTI responses, receipts, contracts, communications).
Submit formal complaint to the State Vigilance / ACB.
If state authorities fail to act or if political influence delays action, escalate to the State Lokayukta (often requires a sworn affidavit on prescribed forms).
For Central Government employees, PSUs, or nationalized banks, file directly on the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) portal or via CPGRAMS.
